title: Support read-only export and workspace projection for tracker-none documentation bundles
summary: Support read-only export and workspace projection for tracker-none documentation bundles
description:
Reported from the cli-test review and Orbitfall project exercise on 2026-09-04. Installed tools: Lore 0.4.1 and Quest 0.3.2, macOS ARM64. Source review revisions: Lore 054e6590f1b81fda418c9891611f84fd35aacf6e; Quest dcb06f6520e08f2755c04166cca168318a94ae5a. Findings describe those tested versions, not a claim that current HEAD was retested. Evidence paths below are retained in the sibling cli-test checkout; the reproduction and outcomes are also included here. Filing is not a fix.

In a fresh disposable Git repository:
  lore init --yes --tracker none
  lore new reference Peer --summary "Documentation-only bundle" --json
  lore sync
  lore validate --strict --json
  lore export --json
Observed: strict validation succeeds, but export exits 6 with "this bundle has issue-tracker coupling disabled". An explicit workspace member using tracker none also fails workspace validation; initializing/selecting Quest for the same member succeeds.
Expected: read-only documentation export/projection represents an empty task set for a valid docs-only bundle. Tracker-dependent writes may still reject disabled coupling. LCLI-343 (Done) enabled tracker-free initialization/configuration; this is the remaining export/workspace read path, not a duplicate request to add none initialization.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A valid tracker-none bundle exports documentation successfully with an empty task projection.
Explicit workspaces can validate and project tracker-none members alongside tracker-enabled members.
Tests cover these read paths and retain clear errors for operations that actually require tracker writes.
